title: "Part 4 – Multiverse, replication and preregistration"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/cohabitation-one-day.html#/part-4-multiverse-replication-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 opens on the chart that the class has just built and reads it against every justifiable analysis of the claim on the rebuilt data. It then turns to the two replications of the paper, which tested two different coefficients, and closes on the single analysis that you would defend, declared before it runs.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Multiverse](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd) and slides | Your own small multiverse, then the curve of the claim: the 144 specifications ranked from the largest decline to the smallest, with the published result of the original authors (OAs) and the analysis of 456AP placed on it. An optional pair of slides tells where the idea of a multiverse came from and draws the garden of forking paths. | 10 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | Find your own mark among the exploratory results of the class. Then rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted and read your placement, the number of the 144 specifications whose estimate lies further below zero than yours, and send it in chat when the facilitator says go. | 10 minutes |
| Slides, with [what moved the estimate](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd#shifts) on the Multiverse page as the follow-up | Each option of the curve set beside its twins, the curve coloured by the cohort window, which carries most of its variance, and what the curve leaves out, above all the construction of the data, which lies upstream of every specification. | 8 minutes |
| Slides, with [the replications](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd#sec-replication) on the case study as the follow-up | The SCORE replication, which tested the interaction of some college and period on later surveys and did not replicate it; the period coefficient of the claim on later surveys rebuilt by the course; the three Rs on this paper; and what the repetitions of this paper found. | 14 minutes |
| Slides, with [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd) as the follow-up | The critics of the multiverse, the argument that a fully specified question has one correct analysis and how anyone would identify it, what preregistration settles and what it leaves open, and the difference between the exploration of Task 4 and the declaration of Task 5. | 8 minutes |
| Slides, with [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) as the follow-up | Where a reanalysis is archived and registered, the preregistration of Multi100 itself, the two preregistration templates, the public record of the case with a three-minute search of the Multi100 component, and the eight AsPredicted questions mapped onto the decisions that you have already met. | 6 minutes |
| The preregistration block in your report, or [Browser lab](../../cases/cohabitation/lab.qmd#task-5-preregistration) Task 5 | Complete the preregistration block before you run anything: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, one option for each of the fifteen decisions, a sentence from your causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Render the report, or on the browser lab page copy the completed cell into your notes, and type "declared" in chat. When the class has declared, fit the specification with `run_spec()` and send it with `report_result()`. Your declared result is drawn on the chart as a filled circle beside the open circles of Task 4. | 26 minutes |
| Slides and [Multiverse](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | Two points from the literature, the single analytical path, what you take with you and the feedback form, with the class chart on screen. | 8 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have your own placement among the 144 specifications of the curve, one specification fixed in the preregistration block of your report before it was run, a report of your own that contains the result of that specification, and a view of what a verdict of 'not replicated' means when the replication tested another coefficient than the one in the claim.
